current_versions.LuaLS/lua-language-server: 3.19.x line seen in primary release listing (3.19.0 release page fetched via search); actively released

current_versions.StyLua: 2.x line in active use (v2.5.2 pinned in multiple Sep 2026 CI references found in search); no primary StyLua release page fetched in this pass, exact latest unverified

error_handling.guide_position: Return (nil, 'descriptive error') for expected failures; never bare pcall(do_work) - capture and propagate
error_handling.best_practice: Lua manual tradition is (nil,msg) / pcall-based; guide's convention is compatible and stricter, not contradicted by any fetched official source
error_handling.evidence: No official source fetched contradicts the (nil,err) convention; it is a Tiger Style strictness choice

bounded_work.guide_position: Bound loops/retries/queues/caches with named *_MAX constants; no unexplained while true
bounded_work.best_practice: No official Lua limit prescribes this; it is deliberate Tiger Style strictness beyond the manual
bounded_work.evidence: Lua 5.5 adds incremental major GC and more compact arrays, which help memory bounds but do not replace application bounds - see 5.5 changes list

assertions_contracts.guide_position: assert() for internal invariants, validation returns for external input; LuaCATS annotations; runtime list stops at 5.4+
assertions_contracts.best_practice: Lua 5.5 adds declarations for global variables and read-only for-loop variables - a language-level contract mechanism the guide never mentions
assertions_contracts.evidence: 5.5 changes list fetched via search: global declarations, named vararg tables, for-loop variables read-only, table.create

memory_ownership.guide_position: GC language: cap caches/queues, one owner per handle, idempotent teardown, table.concat over repeated concatenation
memory_ownership.best_practice: Lua 5.5 itself improves this area: more compact arrays (~60% less for large arrays per changes list) and incremental major GC - guide's 5.4-era GC discussion does not cover either
memory_ownership.evidence: 5.5 changes list in search results quoting lua.org readme

formatting.guide_position: 4-space, 100 cols, stylua.toml with column_width=100, indent_width=4, quote_style AutoPreferSingle
formatting.best_practice: StyLua is the de facto formatter; guide's keys are StyLua keys, but no primary StyLua docs page was fetched in this pass to verify every key/default against the current 2.x line
formatting.evidence: Search showed StyLua v2.5.2 in active CI use but did not fetch stylua.sh / repo docs directly; per audit rule this aspect is unverified rather than asserted

static_analysis.guide_position: luacheck in Sec.27 validation recipe (stylua --check, luacheck, lua tests) plus LuaLS/LuaCATS in the wider diver workflow
static_analysis.best_practice: Luacheck's own README claims syntax support only for Lua 5.1/5.2/5.3/LuaJIT; LuaLS 3.19.x is actively released and is the tool that tracks 5.4/5.5 - relying on luacheck alone leaves a coverage gap for modern syntax
static_analysis.evidence: Luacheck home repo text fetched via search; LuaLS 3.19.0 release page fetched via search

concurrency.guide_position: Coroutines/async: generation tokens, reject stale callbacks, bound outstanding work, revalidate handles after delay
concurrency.best_practice: No fetched official source contradicts this; Neovim vim.uv/vim.system model is host-specific and guide correctly scopes it
concurrency.evidence: Guide correctly treats this as a host/Neovim discipline, not a Lua-language claim

testing.guide_position: Boundary tests {0,1,M-1,M,M+1}, nil/false, malformed, cancellation, stale callbacks, cleanup after failure
testing.best_practice: Compatible with lua.org's own 'make all test' distribution practice; stricter Tiger Style split is not contradicted
testing.evidence: lua.org download page shows upstream ships tests via make all test

toolchain_pins.guide_position: Primary targets: Lua 5.4+, LuaJIT, Neovim Lua, embedded Lua (Version 1.0 guide)
toolchain_pins.best_practice: Current Lua is 5.5 / 5.5.1 as of the fetched download page (2026-07-24). A 5.4+ target that never names 5.5, its global declarations, or its incompatibilities is stale as a current-baseline statement
toolchain_pins.evidence: lua.org download page fetched directly: 'The current version is Lua 5.5 and its current release is Lua 5.5.1'

security.guide_position: Never interpolate untrusted input into shell strings (argv via vim.system), treat load/dofile/package.loadlib/FFI as privileged, empty load() env is not a sandbox
security.best_practice: No fetched official source contradicts this; 5.5 global declarations strengthen, but do not replace, this posture
security.evidence: Guide position is stricter than mainstream Lua practice - by audit rule that is not a contradiction

mechanical_fixes.current: **Primary targets:** Lua 5.4+, LuaJIT, Neovim Lua, embedded Lua
mechanical_fixes.correct: **Primary targets:** Lua 5.5+, LuaJIT, Neovim Lua, embedded Lua (note 5.5 incompatibilities and global-variable declarations; 5.4 remains a supported legacy target where declared)
mechanical_fixes.evidence: lua.org download page fetched 2026-10-14 states current version is Lua 5.5, current release 5.5.1 (2026-07-24)

proposals.proposal: Add a Lua 5.5 section: when the declared runtime is 5.5, prefer/support global-variable declarations and read-only for-loop variables as contract mechanisms, and document the 5.4->5.5 incompatibilities behind the runtime boundary the guide already requires
proposals.evidence: 5.5 changes list: declarations for global variables, named vararg tables, for-loop variables read-only, table.create
proposals.recommendation: Adopt as an optional 5.5 boundary note; do not rewrite 5.4/LuaJIT/Neovim code to require it, since Neovim/LuaJIT do not follow 5.5

proposals.proposal: Demote luacheck from the sole lint gate for 5.4+/5.5 code: state its documented syntax ceiling (5.1-5.3/LuaJIT per its README) and make LuaLS diagnostics (--check with the project's .luarc.json) the primary static gate, with luacheck retained for the undefined-global sweep on syntax it can parse
proposals.evidence: Luacheck README support list vs LuaLS 3.19.x active releases
proposals.recommendation: Adopt wording change in Sec.27/28; keep the existing Matt per-file gate (LuaLS+stylua+luacheck) but document luacheck's ceiling so a parse failure on 5.5 syntax is not misread as a code defect
